1. Overview

Retiam includes a high-performance, cross-engine 2D physics subsystem designed for games, scientific visualizations, and dynamic motion graphics. It provides a unified, engine-agnostic API that transparently drives either:
Both backends seamlessly integrate with Retiam's Entity-Component-System (ECS) scene graph and WebGPU vector rendering pipeline.

blocks.text: 2. Core Architecture
[Physics2D.ts](../libs/physics/2d/Physics2D.ts)
The central manager attached to a `Scene`. It creates the backend instance, manages rigid bodies, spring lattices, constraints, collision dispatching, and pointer interactions.
Engine Parameter Unification: Harmonic Oscillator Formulation
Previously, Planck and Rapier used incompatible parameters for elastic constraints:

items: **Planck / Box2D** uses natural oscillation frequency $f$ (`frequencyHz`) and damping ratio $\zeta$ (`dampingRatio`).
**Rapier** natively expects absolute stiffness $k$ (spring constant) and viscous damping coefficient $c$.

blocks.text: Retiam unifies both engines around standard harmonic oscillator physics:
where $m = \frac{m_1 m_2}{m_1 + m_2}$ is the effective reduced mass of the connected bodies. This guarantees identical spring behavior regardless of which backend is selected.
3. Rigid Bodies & Motion Types
Entities are added to the simulation using `physics.add(entity, options)`.

cells.text: Driven by gravity, contact forces, impulses, and constraints.
Immovable barrier; unaffected by forces or collisions.
Positioned programmatically or via velocity; pushes dynamic objects.

blocks.text: Automatic Geometry Inference
Retiam automatically infers collider shapes from vector primitives:

items: **`Circle`**: Creates a 2D circular collider with matching radius.
**`Rect`**: Creates an axis-aligned box collider using width and height.
**`Poly` / `RegularPolygon`**: Extracts vertices, handles concave decomposition or convex hulls, and sets up matching polygonal colliders.

blocks.text: Configuration Interface ([Physics2DTypes.ts](../libs/physics/2d/Physics2DTypes.ts))

blocks.code:
export interface Rigid2DOptions {
    motion?: 'dynamic' | 'static' | 'kinematic'; // Default: 'dynamic'
    density?: number;        // Fixture density. Default: 1.0
    mass?: number;           // Explicit mass override in kg
    friction?: number;       // Friction coefficient. Default: 0.3
    restitution?: number;    // Restitution / bounciness (0.0 to 1.0). Default: 0.2 (0.6 for circles)
    isSensor?: boolean;      // Non-colliding trigger sensor. Default: false
    lockRotation?: boolean;  // Locks angular rotation. Default: false
    linearDamping?: number; // Linear drag. Default: 0.0
    angularDamping?: number;// Rotational drag. Default: 0.0
    ccd?: boolean;           // Continuous Collision Detection (prevents tunneling). Default: false
    gravityScale?: number;   // Per-body gravity multiplier. Default: 1.0
}

blocks.text: 4. Interactive Mouse Dragging
Retiam 2D physics includes built-in pointer interaction via `physics.enableMouseDrag(options)`.
How It Works

items: Listens to `pointerdown`, `pointermove`, and `pointerup` on the canvas.
Performs a point query or raycast against active physics fixtures.
Dynamically creates a ground-anchored spring joint constraint connected to the selected body at the click point.
Updates the anchor position as the mouse moves, allowing users to grab, drag, swing, and fling bodies.

6. 2D Soft Bodies & Deformable Meshes
Retiam supports real-time deformable soft bodies and elastic mass-spring lattices via `physics.addSoftBody(entity, options)`.
A. Radial Soft Body Blobs (shape: 'radial')
Used for squishy deformable polygons (`Poly`, `Poly.regular(N, radius)`):

items: Instantiates circular colliders at polygon vertices + an internal central hub particle.

items.text: Interconnects particles using a triangulated spoke-wheel topology:
children: **Perimeter Ring Springs**: Maintain the outer closed polygon boundary.

**Rim-Anchored Hub Spokes**: Radial springs connected to the surface of the central hub at exact angles $\alpha_i$, creating angular restoring stiffness that prevents tangential sliding or vertex bunching.
**Triangulated Cross Spokes**: Connects each perimeter particle to adjacent hub rim anchors, eliminating vertex inversion modes and guaranteeing 100% elastic shape recovery under extreme squishing.

blocks.text: B. Grid Lattice Cloth & Curtains (shape: 'grid')
Used for deformable sheets, hanging curtains, and elastic trampolines:

items: Creates a 2D $M \times N$ matrix of particle colliders.

children: **Structural & Shear Springs**: Horizontal, vertical, and cross-diagonal springs.
**Bending Resistance Springs**: Connects particles 2 grid steps away ($r \pm 2, c \pm 2$) to eliminate sharp creases, prevent accordion folding, and maintain planar recovery.

items: Supports anchor pinning: `'top-edge'`, `'corners'`, an array of indices, or a predicate function.

blocks.text: 7. Zero-Gap Contact Alignment Architecture
In physics engines, soft bodies are approximated using an array of circular colliders of radius $r$ (`particleRadius`). This introduces a fundamental geometric challenge:

blocks.code:
[Traditional Approach - Floating Gap]
Visual Vertex = Collider Center
------------------------------------------------------
     (•) Collider Center = Visual Vertex
    /   \
   |  r  |  Collider Perimeter (Collision Surface)
    \___/
====================================================== Floor Surface
     ↑ Gap of size r where object appears to float!

blocks.text: The Retiam Solution
During the ECS update pass, each visual vertex is offset outward from its particle center along the outward surface normal by exactly $+r$:
This expands the visual polygon to lie flush with the **outer contact surface** of the physical circle colliders.

When radial particles are instantiated, they are placed inward by $r$. Combined with the $+r$ outward expansion in the component, the resting geometry matches the author's specified dimensions with mathematical precision.
Soft bodies rest flush on floors, obstacles, and against adjacent stacked bodies with **zero visible gap**.

blocks.code:
[Retiam Zero-Gap Contact Alignment]
Visual Vertex = Collider Center + (Normal * r)
------------------------------------------------------
     (•) Collider Center
    /   \
   |  r  |  
   \__V__/  Visual Vertex == Collision Surface
====================================================== Floor Surface
     No gap! Visual mesh directly touches contact surface.

Enforces a constant distance between two anchor points.

Creates both a physical spring joint and an animated visual `Spring` coil entity.
Welds two bodies together, locking relative translation and rotation.

10. Best Practices & Performance Guidelines

children: Use **`'rapier'`** when simulating hundreds of dynamic bodies or complex compound shapes where WASM SIMD execution excels.
Use **`'planck'`** when zero-dependency, pure JavaScript execution or exact Box2D parity is required.
For stable jelly polygons, use `frequencyHz` between `5.0` and `8.0` with `dampingRatio` between `0.15` and `0.3`.
Avoid setting `frequencyHz > 15.0` on soft bodies without increasing `velocityIterations` / solver sub-steps.
Enable `ccd: true` on fast, small dynamic objects (e.g., pinball projectiles) to prevent tunneling through thin barriers.
Use `collisionGroups` bitmasks to filter out unnecessary collision pairs (e.g., particles within the same soft body that are already constrained by structural springs).
